text:
You need a WordPress solution that limits MB Frontend Submission posts by user role and redirects members to an upgrade page once they hit their submission limit.

Hi, I’m Tobias Reyne. I’d be glad to help you build a stable solution for this requirement, with the goal of keeping it independent from future MetaBox updates.

I understand you’re using MetaBox for custom post types, Elementor for layout/templates, WooCommerce for memberships and subscriptions, and User Role Editor for custom roles and permissions. The core of your request is to control frontend submissions based on role, enforce per-role post limits, and redirect users to a specific page when they can no longer submit. That’s exactly the kind of logic I would structure carefully so it behaves consistently and remains maintainable.

My background is in full stack development with 7 years of experience, and I work with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST API, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS. While your stack is WordPress-focused, the same principles apply here: clean logic, predictable conditions, and code that is designed to be separated from plugin updates as much as possible.

For your case, I would approach this by creating a custom plugin or custom script that checks the current user’s role and submission count before the frontend form is displayed or processed. If the limit has been reached, the plugin can block further submissions and redirect the user to your chosen upgrade URL. If needed, the logic can be mapped to different roles and limits so you can manage membership tiers more easily.

I’d also make sure the solution is straightforward for you to maintain as site administrator, with the role-based rules clearly separated and easy to adjust later. Since you already have the platform structure in place, the main focus would be on making this submission control reliable and compatible with your existing setup.

If you’d like, I can help you turn this into a custom, future-resistant implementation.
